title: OpenWispr vs Muesli — dictation-only + Android vs dictation-plus-meeting-notes, Apple Silicon only
description: OpenWispr vs Muesli: Muesli adds Granola-style local meeting transcription with speaker labels to its dictation, publishes a clear model table, and is Apple Silicon Mac only.
ogDescription: Muesli bundles dictation with local meeting transcription and the clearest published model table in this research. It's Apple Silicon Mac only, with no Android app.
subhead: Muesli is 100% local dictation plus Granola-style meeting transcription with speaker labels — no bot joining your calls. It's macOS 14.2+, Apple Silicon only, with no Android app.

intro.heading: Muesli does more per session; OpenWispr does it on more devices.
paragraphs: Muesli (836 ★, MIT) is dictation plus local meeting transcription with speaker labels, entirely on-device, with no bot joining your calls to capture them. It publishes the clearest model table found in this research — Parakeet v3 (25 languages, ~0.13s), Nemotron 3.5 (100+ locales), Cohere 2B (~1s), and Whisper Large Turbo (~2–4s) — which makes the accuracy/speed tradeoff self-explanatory rather than a guess.

It's macOS 14.2+, Apple Silicon only. There's no Windows, Linux, iOS, or Android build. OpenWispr doesn't currently match its meeting-transcription feature, but it does run on Android and on Intel Macs, neither of which Muesli covers.

sections.heading: A second product bolted cleanly onto dictation, and real transparency
paragraphs: Meeting transcription with speaker labels, running entirely on-device with no bot joining the call, is a meaningfully different capability from single-utterance dictation — and Muesli ships it well. Its published model table is also the clearest thing of its kind found across this whole research effort: four models with size, latency, and language-count spelled out, so "why pick one over another" answers itself instead of requiring trial and error.

Its permission model is worth copying directly: request Accessibility only when it unlocks pasting, Input Monitoring only when it unlocks the hotkey, Screen/Audio only when it unlocks meetings — instead of a wall of dialogs at first launch. That's a better first-run experience than most apps in this category, OpenWispr's current flow included.

sections.heading: Android, and Intel Macs
paragraphs: Muesli requires Apple Silicon specifically — no Intel Mac support, and nothing on Windows, Linux, iOS, or Android. OpenWispr runs on Android today and doesn't require an M-series chip on macOS.
If meeting transcription isn't something you need and your device isn't a Silicon Mac, Muesli isn't reachable at all; OpenWispr is.

faqs.q: Does Muesli have an Android app?
faqs.a: No. Muesli is macOS 14.2+, Apple Silicon only, with no build for Windows, Linux, iOS, or Android. OpenWispr's Android app is live on Google Play.

faqs.q: Does OpenWispr do meeting transcription like Muesli?
faqs.a: Not today. Muesli's local, Granola-style meeting transcription with speaker labels is a distinct, well-built feature OpenWispr doesn't currently match.

faqs.q: Does Muesli work on an Intel Mac?
faqs.a: No — Apple Silicon only. OpenWispr supports both Intel and Apple Silicon Macs.

Per their own published table: Parakeet v3 (25 languages, ~0.13s), Nemotron 3.5 (100+ locales), Cohere 2B (~1s), and Whisper Large Turbo (~2–4s) — the clearest model documentation found in this research. OpenWispr currently ships NVIDIA Parakeet-TDT by default or Whisper via whisper.cpp, selectable, without the same published latency table yet.
